newsitem.title: USA: Cinergy able to partially offset weather.
newsitem.headline: Cinergy able to partially offset weather.

text.p: Cinergy Corp said Friday it was able to offset much of the drag of cooler weather with growth and cost controls, leaving second quarter earnings per share unchanged from a year ago at $0.35.

Net income was $55.5 million in the latest quarter compared with $56 million in the second quarter a year ago, which included a write-off of $17.4 million, or $0.07 per share, for voluntary workforce reduction programs.

It said higher earnings in 1997 from rate increases and savings from the workforce reduction programs were more than offset by the reduction in retail kilowatthour sales from the unusually mild weather during the second quarter.
This May was the third coldest on record in the company's service area, and 1997 set a record for the number of days before reaching a temperature of 90 degrees, it explained.

"While we have experienced weather impacts on earnings as have other energy services companies, continued growth in the region and our ability to control costs helped mitigate its impact," said James E. Rogers, Cinergy chief executive officer.

The utility said growth of more than 400 percent over the prior year in power sales and trading volumes by its Energy Commodities Business Unit resulted in an increase in total electric power sales of 65.5 percent in the second quarter compared with a year earlier.
Gas sales and transportation volumes for the quarter ended June 30 increased 1.8 percent when compared to the same period in 1996, Cinergy said.
